seed_id: topic:How do few-shot example order and class imbalance affect pretrained language-model classification, and does balancing example labels improve worst-order performance at a fixed prompt length?

idea.title: Investigating the Joint Impact of Few-Shot Example Order and Class Imbalance on Pretrained Language Model Classification Robustness
idea.research_problem: Pretrained language models exhibit high sensitivity to the ordering and composition of in-context few-shot demonstration examples, particularly under conditions of class imbalance. However, the interaction between demonstration ordering sensitivity and class label distribution skew remains unquantified for text classification.
idea.research_gap: Bounded search findings indicate that while prompt sensitivity metrics and cross-lingual example selection have been studied, the combined influence of class imbalance within the few-shot demonstration bank and sequence ordering on worst-case prediction variance is unexplored for mid-to-low resource text classification.
idea.methodology: We operationalize demonstration sensitivity by systematically varying example order permutations and class imbalance ratios in the prompt context. Using a fixed prompt length, we construct balanced versus imbalanced demonstration subsets. We measure the variance in classification accuracy and label bias across permutations using an off-the-shelf instruction-tuned model via API access or local inference on a 12GB consumer GPU.
idea.expected_contribution: We hypothesize that enforcing label balance within the few-shot demonstration subset significantly reduces prompt ordering sensitivity and improves worst-case classification performance compared to naturally skewed demonstration sets.
idea.experimental_setup: We evaluate on a public text classification dataset (e.g., AG News or a publicly accessible multi-class text benchmark) using a 4-shot and 8-shot setting. We test 24 distinct permutations of example orderings under both balanced and heavily imbalanced class distributions, keeping total token length strictly constant across conditions.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We report mean accuracy, standard deviation across permutations (sensitivity metric), and worst-case (minimum) accuracy. We split data into a calibration set of 200 samples for prompt template selection and a held-out test set of 1,000 samples. Statistical significance is assessed using paired permutation tests with a confidence threshold of p < 0.05.
feasibility_assumptions: Pretrained models accessed via API or local 12GB GPU can reliably output token log-probabilities or discrete predictions for all permutations.
Publicly available benchmark texts can be truncated to fit fixed prompt length constraints without losing gold-label semantics.
Permutation testing across 24 orderings fits within inference time and API rate limits for the 1,000 test instances.

assumption_checks.assumption: API or local model inference latency allows running 24 order permutations across 1,000 test instances within standard evaluation timeframes.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Run a pilot test measuring inference time for 50 instances across all 24 permutations.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Total pilot execution completes under 30 minutes.
assumption_checks.fallback: Reduce the evaluated permutation sample space to 8 representative orderings using Latin hypercube sampling.

assumption_checks.assumption: Fixed prompt length truncation does not systematically distort class label representations in the demonstration set.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Inspect token counts and semantic overlap scores of truncated versus full demonstration texts.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Cosine similarity between full and truncated text embeddings remains above 0.85.
assumption_checks.fallback: Adjust the maximum token budget upward to accommodate untruncated shortest-quartile examples.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Evaluates prompt sensitivity and consistency metrics across prompt rephrasings for text classification.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Focuses on demonstration example ordering permutations and class imbalance interaction rather than surface prompt rephrasings.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Confirm that ordering variance metrics correlate with or act orthogonally to rephrasing sensitivity.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Optimizes few-shot demonstration selection and example bank retrieval for low-resource settings.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Examines explicit class balance constraints within a fixed-length prompt rather than cross-lingual example retrieval banks.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Test whether balancing existing retrieved sets further mitigates worst-order performance drops.

idea.core_hypothesis: Enforcing uniform class label distribution among few-shot in-context examples significantly decreases performance variance across random demonstration orderings compared to imbalanced distributions.
idea.distinctive_mechanism: Controlled manipulation of class label counts within a constant-length demonstration sequence to isolate the effect of label balance on sequence-position bias.
idea.minimum_test: Compare the variance of classification accuracy across 24 fixed-length order permutations between a balanced 4-shot prompt and an imbalanced 4-shot prompt on a 200-sample validation subset.
